names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 11 octombrie, «Sfântul Apostol Filip, unul din cei 7 diaconi».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιος Φίλιππος ο Απόστολος ένας από τους επτά Διακόνους», with the rank words left off.
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2292, headed «Святой Филипп, апостол от 70-ти», with the rank word and the office left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 11. октобар ст. ст., „Св. апостол Филип.“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank and апостол is the `apostle` this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. The heading gives him no epithet and nothing that would tell him from the Philip of the Twelve; the body is what identifies him. `foldchk.py` measured the string as held by `philip-of-moscow` alone before this day, and the two-folder fold is read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

feast.note: Both of the site's lives for him head «Дни памяти: 4 января (70 ап.) , 11 октября» — this day and the synaxis of the Seventy Apostles. One row per church is the schema, so the January day is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 11 октября ст. ст. — «Ап. Филиппа , единого от семи диаконов (I).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the first of the day's two icons, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — the plain service — which stands immediately before his line. The day carries a second icon of the same kind a few words later, before Theophanes of Nicaea, and the two lines after that, Leo of Optina and the Optina synaxis, carry none.

attestations.note: The Russian's «(I)» is the first century and no year is given on either of its two lives, so no `dates` are proposed. Its index page heads him «Святой Филипп, апостол от 70-ти», of the Seventy, where the day line calls him one of the seven deacons; both are his. The two lives differ in where they end him: the first has the apostles ordain him bishop at Jerusalem and send him to Lydia, the second to Tralles in Lydia, and both have him die in deep old age. The second also carries the detail from Acts the first leaves out, that an angel caught him away to Azotus after the eunuch's baptism.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 11 octombrie — «Sfântul Apostol Filip, unul din cei 7 diaconi»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Φίλιππος ο Απόστολος ένας από τους επτά Διακόνους»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the deacon of Caesarea in Palestine, one of the seven of Acts 6, married with four prophesying daughters of Acts 21.8–9, who preached in Samaria. The page gives no year, so no `dates` object is proposed. It records part of his skull at the monastery of Saint John the Theologian on Patmos. It prints a proper apolytikion naming him and a kontakion addressed to him as Ἀπόστολε, both taken here; it also prints an «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον», the short common «Ἀπόστολε Ἅγιε Φίλιππε», and a Κάθισμα, neither of which is drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 24.10.2026 (11. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. апостол Филип.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted whole, with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because srbody.mjs and sr-cand.mjs both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends ". " in the source. **THE HEADING SAYS апостол AND THE MAN IS THE DEACON, AND THE BODY IS WHAT SETTLES IT.** The corpus holds a Philip of the Twelve as well, so the heading alone would be ambiguous; the entry identifies him outright — born at Caesarea in Palestine, married with four daughters, chosen a deacon when the apostles chose the deacons **beside Stephen and the rest**, server of the poor and the widows, preacher in Samaria, baptiser of Simon Magus and of the eunuch of queen Candace, carried off by an angel to Azotus, and made bishop in Tralles. That is this folder’s man line for line, and the `apostle` the heading gives him is already in its `types` beside `deacon` and `bishop`. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. **All four daughters are said to have been given the gift of prophecy and all four to have vowed virginity for Christ’s sake**, where the other books count them. **The angel carried him to Azotus тренутно и невидљиво**, in an instant and invisibly. And the see is Тралија, Tralles, which the folder already holds from another book and which **is not written into `office`** here: a scalar field is not improved by a second book repeating it, and nothing in the entry grades the see. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND UNTOUCHABLE: the folder holds `dates: null` and this entry gives no year, only «Сконча мирно у дубокој старости», in deep old age — **and an age is not a date and a lifespan is refused**. The appended paragraph carries no four-digit year at all; with neither birth nor death on the folder, `date-audit`’s `stated` reads its prose for both. Measured after the write: unmoved. `related` UNTOUCHED, AND EVERY PERSON THE ENTRY NAMES WHO HAS A FOLDER IS ALREADY THERE: `stephen-the-first-martyr`, `the-eunuch-of-queen-candace`, `paul-the-apostle` and `john-the-theologian`. **Simon Magus takes no row and is not a corpus saint**; queen Candace is the eunuch’s mistress and not a relation. No `locations`. THE FOLD THIS ENTRY MADE: `foldchk.py` measured «Филип» before the day as `[('philip-of-moscow', 'sr')]`, so it goes from one folder to two and the key is written into `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in the same commit. The other is the metropolitan of Moscow and All Russia, 1507 to 1569, kept on 9 January. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S SECOND ENTRY IS REFUSED AND IT IS NOT A CLOSE CALL. «Спомен Седмог Васељенског Сабора.» — **a Council is not a folder**, and the entry is about the Council and not about a person: Nicaea in 787 under the empress Irene and her son Constantine and the patriarch Tarasius, 367 Fathers, the definition of the veneration of icons out of Scripture, the Fathers and attested wonders, and the ruling that relics of martyrs must be put into the antimension. It names the bishop Constantine of Cyprus, who told the Council the story of the shepherd of Constantia who struck the Mother of God’s icon with his iron staff, spoiled the right eye of the image, stumbled on leaving and put out his own right eye with the same staff. **None of those takes a row and none is in any prose of this day**: the Fathers of a Council are not a folder, an emperor in an entry is not a relation, and the subject of an anecdote told at a Council is further still from one. `tarasius-of-constantinople` has a folder and gets nothing from this day.

hymns.text: Apostole Sfinte Filip, roagă pe Milostivul Dumnezeu, ca să dăruiască iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Apostol Filip, unul din cei 7 diaconi

english.text: O holy Apostle Philip, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of sins.

hymns.text: Θείας χάριτος, πλήρης ὑπάρχων, διηκόνησας, τὴ Ἐκκλησία, ὡς Διάκονος Τοῦ Λόγου Ἀπόστολε, θεοσημείαις δὲ θείαις χρησάμενος, τῆς Σαμαρείας τὰ πλήθη κατηύγασας. Μάκαρ Φίλιππε, Χριστὸν τὸν θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ἠμὶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Φίλιππος ο Απόστολος ένας από τους επτά Διακόνους», and it names him.

english.text: Being full of divine grace, you served the Church as a deacon of the Word, Apostle; and using divine signs from God you lit up the multitudes of Samaria. Blessed Philip, entreat Christ our God to grant us his great mercy.

hymns.text: Μιμητὴς γενόμενος, τοῦ Διδασκάλου, δι' αὐτὸν Ἀπόστολε, ταὶς τῶν Ἁγίων τῶν αὐτοῦ, χρείαις πιστῶς διηκόνησας, ὅθεν σὲ πάντες, πιστοὶ μακαρίζομεν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ', Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον — on the page of «Άγιος Φίλιππος ο Απόστολος ένας από τους επτά Διακόνους». It addresses him as Ἀπόστολε and names no other saint.

english.text: Having become an imitator of the Teacher, for his sake, Apostle, you served faithfully the needs of his saints; and so all we faithful call you blessed.
